segments.he: עַל יְדֵי צְעָקָה יְכוֹלִים לְהִתְקָרֵב לַה' יִתְבָּרַךְ אַף מִשְּׁאוֹל
segments.en: Even though one must hasten greatly to save one's soul from what one needs to be saved from — even so, when one sees that one's redemption is greatly delayed, one must strengthen oneself to wait greatly for His salvation until He looks down from Heaven and sees, as it is written: "and I will always hope" [Tehillim 71:14]. And as it is in the matter of the collective redemption of Yisrael — where certainly one must fall on one's face each day and weep and beseech greatly before Him to hasten our redemption immediately, for the exile has long been upon us and the strength of the bearer has weakened — even so, when one sees that the exile extends further, one must wait more and more, as it is written: "if it delays, wait for it — for it will surely come, it will not be late" [Chavakkuk 2:3]. So too individually for every person — even though one must weep greatly before Hashem and beseech before Him for one's soul to redeem it speedily from the desires and vanities of this world, even so when one sees that the matter is greatly delayed, one must hope and wait greatly, time after time, perhaps He will see one's affliction — for He does not contend forever and does not remain angry for eternity. And even though the obstacle is from our side, because our deeds are not as they should be — even as one is — even so, as long as one lifts one's eyes above and guards and awaits and waits for His salvation, through this very act Hashem will take pity and have compassion and draw one close to His service in truth — and everything will be transformed for good.

segments.he: יֵשׁ בְּנֵי אָדָם שֶׁרְחוֹקִים מְאד מְאד מֵה' יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּתַכְלִית הָרִחוּק וּמֻנָּחִים בִּשְׁאוֹל תַּחְתִּיּוֹת מַמָּשׁ. וּכְשֶׁמִּתְעוֹרְרִים וְרוֹצִים לַעֲשׂוֹת תְּשׁוּבָה אֵין לָהֶם שׁוּם עֵצָה וְתַחְבּוּלָה וּצְרִיכִים רַק לְקַיֵּם בְּחִינַת דּם לַה' וּצְרִיכִים לִצְעק מֵעמֶק הַלֵּב לַה' יִתְבָּרַךְ בִּבְחִינַת קוֹל שׁוֹפָר הַנַּ"ל וְעַל יְדֵי בְּחִינָה זוֹ בְּחִינַת דּם לַה' שֶׁהוּא בִּבְחִינַת שׁוֹפָר. עַל יְדֵי זֶה יְכוֹלִים לְהִתְקָרֵב וְלַחֲזר לַה' יִתְבָּרַךְ אֲפִלּוּ הָרְחוֹקִים מְאד כִּי ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ מָלֵא רַחֲמִים וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהֵם רְחוֹקִים כָּל כָּךְ עַד שֶׁאֵינָם יְכוֹלִים לְדַבֵּר שׁוּם דִּבּוּר הָגוּן לִפְנֵי ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ.
segments.en: The practical principle that emerges is that a person must guard himself very greatly from evil longings, and accustom his thought always to long and desire only good longings — to yearn and desire and long always to draw close to Hashem and to His Torah and service. And even when thoughts and impulses of desires and longings for worldly vanities come upon him, let him accustom himself to grab his thought and divert it from these longings — and draw it to good longings, which are the true good forever and eternally. For thought is in the person's hand — to direct it wherever one wishes.

segments.he: אַף עַל פִּי כֵן הֵם מְחֻיָּבִים לִבְלִי לְיָאֵשׁ עַצְמָן חַס וְשָׁלוֹם חַס וְשָׁלוֹם רַק לְצַפּוֹת לִתְשׁוּעַת ה' בִּבְחִינַת טוֹב וְיָחִיל וְדוּמָם לִתְשׁוּעַת ה'. בִּבְחִינַת יֵשֵׁב בָּדָד וְיִדּם כִּי נָטַל עָלָיו (אֵיכָה ג') כִּי עַל יְדֵי הַדְּמִימָה וְהַשְּׁתִיקָה זוֹכֶה לְקַבֵּל מִנְּקֻדָּה הָעֶלְיוֹנָה שֶׁמְּאִירָה בִּנְקֻדָּה הַתַּחְתּוֹנָה. וְזֶה בְּחִינַת כִּי נָטַל עָלָיו. וְעַל כֵּן עַל יְדֵי הַשּׁוֹפָר שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת דּם לַה' שֶׁאֵין יְכוֹלִים לְדַבֵּר כְּלָל רַק שֶׁצּוֹעֲקִים מֵעמֶק הַלֵּב עַל יְדֵי זֶה נִתְקַיֵּם וְאַצִּיעָה שְׁאוֹל הִנֶּךָּ שֶׁיְּכוֹלִים לִמְצא אֶת ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ אֲפִלּוּ בִּשְׁאוֹל תַּחְתִּיּוֹת חַס וְשָׁלוֹם וּמִשָּׁם יְכוֹלִים לְהִתְקָרֵב אֵלָיו כָּל הַנִּדָּחִים וְהַנֶּאֱבָדִים. (הִלְכוֹת ראשׁ הַשָּׁנָה הֲלָכָה דאות ד):
segments.en: And even more must one guard speech — for there is the primary bringing forth of the soul from potential to actuality, for good or the opposite, Heaven forbid. Therefore one must guard oneself very greatly from speaking any evil word, Heaven forbid — at the very least not to bring forth from one's mouth the desires and longings for worldly vanities that come into one's heart. Rather reverse the matter and bring forth with one's mouth good longings. For through speech of good longings, good souls are brought from potential to actuality and form the letters of the Torah for good — to perform good deeds and draw all blessings and divine flows into the world. And these good souls go into the world and arouse the whole world to Hashem and His Torah. And the opposite of the opposite, Heaven forbid. And all this is the matter of hisbodidus and conversation between oneself and one's Maker — to greatly accustom oneself in this, meaning to accustom oneself to long and desire always good longings: when will one merit to turn from evil and do good in His eyes always? And to bring these longings forth with one's mouth each day — and through this one will merit to be saved from the paths of the violent, and only Hashem will support one's steps on His paths.
